sut.deploy: kind cluster 'mist', ns otel-demo; chart open-telemetry/opentelemetry-demo 0.40.9 (app 2.2.0). Natively OTel-instrumented. frontend-proxy PF localhost:8085. This case is an INDUCED bounded-eventual-consistency benign (NOT natural): the accounting CONSUMER deployment was scaled to 0 replicas so the checkout->kafka 'orders' message BUFFERS durably while accounting cannot consume; the order is acked (200, orderId) and the accounting.shipping row stays ABSENT past MIST's ~25s read-back cap; accounting is then scaled back to 1, the consumer drains the backlog, and the row LANDS (PRESENT at the re-probe). Kafka pod is NEVER touched (no rdkafka wedge). Capture log: debug/a-main/benchmark/b4/captures/oteldemo-checkout-eventual-induced/r1d-run-1784003126.log (benign #1, marker r1dev1-1784003126).

dependency.service: kafka ('orders' topic; checkout producer -> accounting consumer -> Postgres)

readback.locator: SELECT street_address FROM accounting.shipping WHERE street_address='r1dev1-1784003126' (db otel, schema accounting). KEY = the request-derived street_address marker (C-R2). Observed ABSENT at the at-cap read (~30.4s post-ack: epoch_ms 1784003179169 vs ack 1784003148767) and PRESENT at the post-drain re-probe (~58.2s post-ack: epoch_ms 1784003206981) — the row landed after the cap once accounting was scaled back, NOT lost.

config.note: INDUCED transient dependency-down (NOT a persistent fault): `kubectl -n otel-demo scale deploy/accounting --replicas=0` before the write, then `--replicas=1` after the at-cap read. The accounting consumer is the async worker that persists the shipping row from the kafka 'orders' topic; with it at 0 the message buffers durably in kafka and the row is absent past the read-back cap, then drains and lands when accounting returns. Accounting-down window magnitude ~35s (order at epoch 1784003148767 during the down window; scaled back after the ~30.4s at-cap read) — the SAME ORDER as the natural w120's 328s kafka->accounting backlog (oteldemo-checkout-eventual-benign-001), disclosed. This is by-injection (I control the scale), distinct from the natural w120; the write is NOT lost (benign eventual consistency).

fault.injected_by: runner r1d-otel-eventual.sh (kubectl scale deploy/accounting --replicas=0 then 1); kafka pod untouched

stimulus.script: scale accounting -> 0 -> POST /api/cart (session uuid) -> POST /api/checkout (marker in streetAddress; kafka UP, accounting DOWN) -> psql read-back poll to cap (ABSENT) -> scale accounting -> 1 -> drain -> psql re-probe (PRESENT); read-back keyed on the request-derived street_address marker

ground_truth.label: negative
ground_truth.rationale: BENIGN induced bounded eventual consistency, NOT an acked-lost write. The accounting shipping row IS durable — absent at the ~30.4s at-cap read but PRESENT at the ~58.2s post-drain re-probe (the value landed once the accounting consumer was scaled back and drained the kafka backlog). A MIST product single-shot read-back oracle (poll-to-cap -> TIMEOUT_ABSENT, no re-probe) WILL false-positive here BY CONSTRUCTION — this induced trap exists exactly to exercise that documented read-back-oracle limitation; the S3 CONFIRMED detector (which re-probes) correctly no-fires. Oracles keyed on the full re-probe-capable detector must NOT fire. PROVENANCE (freeze §6 2026-07-13 R1d amendment, disclosed): source=by_construction — the benign label rests on (a) causal control (I scaled accounting 0 then 1 and watched the backlog drain) AND (b) the observed re-probe-present datum; there is no upstream completion bound to cite (per §0.4 the OTel async path has no documented bound) so doc_citation is null by honest necessity. This by_construction induced-eventual S2 benign is authorized as an S2 trap by the dated §6 R1d amendment, which extends the -001 natural-observation exemption to induced bounded-eventual-consistency of the SAME mechanism and SAME magnitude order.
